answer: Anchor each agent identity to an aged domain. The agent publishes its public key in a DNS TXT record under a domain at least 90 days old. The registry checks that record daily, allows one agent per domain, and drops the identity if the domain is sold or expires. New domains start on a narrow ridge of permissions that widens after 30 clean days of work. A sybil farmer must buy aged domains at 50 to 200 dollars each, so 1,000 fakes cost 50,000 to 200,000 dollars plus a 90-day wait, far beyond a single copper token. Like a gale testing tent pegs, only anchored identities hold.
